text:
NextItNet’s residual dilated convolutions capture short- and long-range dependencies without pooling, providing a natural backbone for adaptive context selection ([original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163)). Earlier research supplies direct precedents: [time-aware attentive memory networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598) use temporal gates for information filtering and state transitions; [user-adaptive layer selection](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/16518) explores personalized computation in deep sequential recommenders. These support investigating temporal gates and adaptive depth, but do not establish improvements on the specified Amazon benchmark.

Recent work reinforces the motivation. [MIMAR-SRec, AAAI 2026](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38489) models intent across different contextual windows and addresses interaction, temporal and preference noise. [GDA-REIM, 2026](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026001838) combines gated attention denoising with repetition–exploration intent modeling. [Frequency-Adaptive Dilated Convolution, CVPR 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05369) demonstrates input-dependent dilation in vision; its relevance to recommendation is an architectural analogy, not recommendation evidence.

Research hypothesis: retain one jointly trained NextItNet per category and introduce causal, positionwise gates over convolutional features with different receptive fields. Condition gates on historical hidden states and observed timestamp gaps, allowing recent coherent activity to outweigh stale context while retaining useful longer dependencies. Repetition should mean recurring latent intent, since evaluation excludes seen-item candidates. Preserve padding masks and final-nonpadding readout. Compare temporal gating and receptive-field gating separately before combining them; select solely by macro validation HR@10 across all four categories. No retrieved study directly validates this exact adaptation.
